newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sells Colbun stake to consortium.
newsitem.headline: Chile sells Colbun stake to consortium.

text.p: Chile has agreed to sell 37.5 percent of state power utility Colbun to a Belgian-Spanish-Chilean group for $340.8 million, the state companies authority CORFO said.
The sale came five days after CORFO rejected the group's previous bid for Colbun, Chile's last state-controlled power company, saying it wasn't high enough.
The winning offer came from a consortium made up of Chilean firm Minera Valparaiso SA and Inversora Electrica Andina, itself comprised of Powerfin, Iberdrola SA and local firm Enagas SA.
The price per share works out to about 50 pesos, equal to the minimum price established by CORFO for the sale, said CORFO General Manager Eduardo Bitran.
Colbun's minority shares on the Santiago Stock Exchange ros early on local news reports that a deal was near.
